detail.body:
### What does this PR do? Adds end-to-end **MXFP8 reinforcement learning on Blackwell (SM100)** to verl, for #5972: Megatron/Transformer Engine (TE) training with `fp8_recipe: mxfp8`, and MXFP8 rollout on **vLLM** and **SGLang**, for dense and MoE models. The design goal is train–inference consistency by construction: the sampler serves the learner's FP8 weight grid (E4M3 elements, one E8M0 scale per 32-element block along K), not an independent re-quantization ("shared-grid" sync). - **In the B200 runs below**, the synced weights were quantized with **TE's own `MXFP8Quantizer`**, the function the learner applies to the weight operand of its forward GEMMs. - **Since the rebase on #8287**, the trainer-side compressed-tensors exporter does it. It uses the same grid and the same shared exponent, except at blocks whose amax is exactly `448 * 2**k`, where compressed-tensors picks the next one up. The bytes of 0.4–0.6% of the blocks change; dequantized values change only below `amax / 14336`, by at most about `4.4e-6 * amax`. | Part | What this PR adds | |---|---| | Training | `fp8_recipe: mxfp8` through the existing `override_transformer_config`. The one functional gap was THD sequence padding: TE's MXFP8 quantizer needs both GEMM dimensions divisible by 32, and the wgrad scale blocks run along the token dimension, so the per-sequence alignment becomes `lcm(32, align)` under MXFP8 (blockwise keeps `lcm(16, align)`). | | vLLM rollout | Served by #8287's compressed-tensors MXFP8 path (`rollout.quantization`), whose trainer-side exporter puts the weights on the learner's grid. This PR adds the post-sync self-check on vLLM's compressed-tensors MXFP8 classes and the audit's engine query. | | SGLang rollout | SGLang has no compressed-tensors MXFP8 scheme, so it is launched with its native MXFP8 method (`quant_method: mxfp8`, `--quantization mxfp8`), and the trainer exports that method's tensor names. A refit loader re-derives the kernel scale layouts once per sync. | | Guards | A self-check after every sync (one dense layer and one MoE expert against a dequantized BF16 reference), a quantized-layer audit (learner vs. exported weights vs. live engine, per weight), and a step sentinel (NaN / KL > 1 / all responses truncated). All are no-ops unless the rollout is quantized. | Nothing changes unless MXFP8 is configured. Related: #5972, #4223, #5440, #7186. Fixes found while validating this PR and merged separately: #7986, #7987, #8062. **Rebased on #8287 (10/20/2026).** #8287 unified low-precision rollout. `rollout.quantization` now takes a preset per layer kind (`linear`, `moe`), and the trainer quantizes rollout weights itself while exporting them, with compressed-tensors. This PR builds on that interface: - **vLLM** serves MXFP8 through #8287's compressed-tensors path. - This PR's ModelOpt MXFP8 vLLM path and its exclusion matcher (#8129, #7918) are dropped. - The exporter's compressed-tensors quantizer puts the weights on the learner's grid; it differs from TE's only at the exponent boundary described above. An earlier version of this rebase used TE's quantizer for those weights to keep them byte-identical; it was dropped as not worth a second numerics path in the exporter. - **SGLang** has no compressed-tensors MXFP8 scheme, so it is served through its native MXFP8 method, with this PR's refit loader. - **Guards.** The self-check and the audit are ported to the new classes, and the audit now compares training, the exported weights and the engine's quant methods. - **Evidence status.** The B200 results below were measured before the rebase, with vLLM on the ModelOpt path. This version has passed the CPU tests but has not been re-run on B200 yet. The split PRs merge into main; this PR stays open for review of the whole: #8127 → #8130 → #8131 → #8132, plus #8128 on its own. ### Results at a glance Measured on NVIDIA B200 with Qwen3-8B (dense) and Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE), in four settings plus 17 controlled runs, before the rebase on #8287. Each configuration ran once (one seed), for 3–60 steps, so nothing here ranks final model quality. 1. **Matching buys consistency.** For an MXFP8 learner, an MXFP8 sampler on the learner's grid is *more* consistent than a BF16 sampler. - In one engine at fixed weights, train–rollout KL is **10.6% lower** with the sampler's qkv/o/down projections on the grid and **16.1% lower** [95% CI 14.1, 18.1] with every linear on the grid. - With TE's quantizer on the sync, as in these runs, the synced weights equalled the learner's FP8 forward weights **byte for byte**. The compressed-tensors exporter used since the rebase differs only at the exponent boundary. - On MoE, verl's existing FP8-blockwise pipeline, whose sampler rounds onto a different grid, has **2×** the MXFP8 pipeline's KL from step 1. - BF16 end to end remains 2.5–10× more consistent. 2. **Speed is conditional.** - MXFP8 cuts the learner's per-token cost (`update_actor` −43%), but adds a fixed **cost per micro-batch** (~51 ms per forward–backward micro-batch), so it pays off only above **~4.5k tokens per micro-batch**. - A sweep on identical replayed data confirms the per-micro-batch form. A trace shows the GPU idle, **waiting for the host to issue work**, for most of the added time. - End to end: MoE step **−10.7%** (generation −24%), dense long-sequence step −6.4%, dense short-sequence step **+5.1%**. 3. **Correctness must be checked against the live engine.** - Seven failures surfaced on B200; five were silent (exit 0, normal-looking metrics). - Each of the four silent failures that reached a run is caught by at least one guard. The two that occurred after the guards were in place were caught at their first opportunity, each by a different guard, and a divergence alarm alone would have missed both. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+mxfp8 - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+5972+in%3Abody - **Not a duplicate.** - **#7186** (draft) adds MXFP8 SGLang rollout with an independent Triton quantizer. This PR differs in three ways: - it puts the rollout weights on the learner's grid (measured byte for byte below, with TE's quantizer on the sync before the rebase); - it ships the training side and both rollout engines as one mode; - it reuses verl's existing FP8 rollout machinery instead of parallel paths. - **#8287** unified the low-precision rollout interface; this PR builds on it (SGLang MXFP8, the guards) and does not duplicate it. - **#7918** was this PR's exact exclusion matcher for vLLM's ModelOpt MXFP8 config; #8287's compressed-tensors path supersedes it, and it will be closed after the B200 re-validation. - **#7971** (draft) is NVFP4, a different format. - The Ascend MXFP8 PRs (#4679, #5608) touch only NPU paths. - [x] PR title formatted as `[megatron, rollout] feat: MXFP8 training and SGLang/vLLM rollout` ### Test CPU unit tests. The first eight files are added in this PR, and the last three are existing tests of the vLLM refit path it extends. TE, vLLM and SGLang are stubbed where needed; compressed-tensors 0.17.0 is installed (without it, 4 of these tests are skipped). ```bash python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_fp8_padding_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_sglang_mxfp8_refit_loader_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp8_refit_check_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_quant_layer_audit_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_quant_sentinel_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_vllm_fp8_restage_same_shape_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_unquant_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_vllm_mxfp4_restage_on_cpu.py -q # 160 passed # existing tests of the training and QAT paths this PR touches: python -m pytest tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py tests/utils/test_config_router_replay_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/test_modelopt_mxfp8_on_cpu.py tests/workers/engine/megatron/test_router_replay_utils_on_cpu.py \ tests/utils/megatron/test_router_replay_model_walk_on_cpu.py -q # 94 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed ``` The one failure, `test_modelopt_mxfp8_on_cpu.py::test_nvfp4_qat_uses_experts_only_export_compatible_backends`, fails the same way on main (4a9dc911) in the same environment (ModelOpt 0.46.0). `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files. The B200 end-to-end runs below predate the rebase. ### B200 validation #### Setup | | A | B | C | D | Controlled runs | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Model | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8) | Qwen3-8B | | Data | gsm8k | DAPO-Math-17k | gsm8k | DAPO-Math-17k | gsm8k | | GPUs | 2×B200, TP2 | 2×B200, TP2 | 2×B200, TP2 | 4×B200, TP2 × EP2 | 2×B200, TP2 | | Rollout | vLLM 0.24 | vLLM 0.24, fp8 KV cache (all arms) | SGLang 0.5.12 | vLLM 0.24 | vLLM 0.24 | | Response cap | 2048 | 8192 | 2048 | 8192 | 2048 | | Steps | 60 | 32 | 30 | 10 | 3–12 | "X/Y" below means learner precision X, sampler precision Y; FP8-TW is TE's per-tensor FP8 and FP8-BW verl's FP8 end-to-end blockwise recipe. - **Shared by all runs:** GRPO, 64 prompts × 8 samples per step, mini-batch 32 prompts, lr 1e-6, KL loss 0.001 (`low_var_kl`), and the same seed and data order within a setting. - **Arms per setting:** - A–C: BF16/BF16, FP8-TW/BF16 and MXFP8/MXFP8. - A also has MXFP8/BF16, the MXFP8 learner with an unquantized sampler. - D adds FP8-BW/FP8-BW. - **Partial matching in A and B.** The vLLM sampler there kept `gate_up_proj` in BF16, through the exclusion bug F2 that this PR fixes. The SGLang (C) and MoE (D) samplers put every decoder linear on the grid, and the controlled matching experiment adds a fully matched vLLM sampler. - **The controlled runs** use A's configuration, with two designs: - a **matching experiment**: four samplers at learning rate 0, so the weights stay at the checkpoint; - a **micro-batch sweep**: replayed identical data, update micro-batches of 1, 2, 4 and 8 sequences plus a half batch, for a BF16 and an MXFP8 learner, with two Nsight Systems profiling runs. - **Statistics.** - Intervals come from bootstrapping prompts within one run per arm. - "±" values are within-run standard errors. - None of these replaces independent seeds. #### 1. Consistency: what matching buys **Controlled matching experiment.** The setup: - one engine (vLLM) and one MXFP8 learner recipe, at learning rate 0, with the same 64 prompts per step in every arm; - the samplers differ only in how many decoder linears are on the learner's grid; - KL is pooled over steps 2–10 (576 prompts × 8 samples), with 95% intervals from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of prompts, paired across arms. | Sampler | KL, step 1 | KL | KL reduction vs. BF16 sampler | k3 reduction | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16/BF16 (reference) | 0.00067 | 0.00072 | | | | MXFP8 learner, BF16 sampler | 0.00854 | 0.00812 | | | | MXFP8/MXFP8, `gate_up_proj` in BF16 | 0.00719 | 0.00726 | 10.6% [8.6, 12.7] | 10.2% [8.7, 11.7] | | MXFP8/MXFP8, every linear on the grid | 0.00697 | 0.00682 | **16.1% [14.1, 18.1]** | 15.5% [14.1, 16.9] | - **What the reduction measures.** The fully matched sampler is 6.1% [3.9, 8.3] below the partially matched one. Log-perplexity and Pearson correlation agree; token-level χ² agrees in direction, but its intervals include zero for each single step of matching. Putting a layer on the grid changes its weights, the quantization of its input activations and its GEMM kernel at once, so the 16% belongs to the recipe as a whole, not to the weight grid alone. - **Byte check.** Bytes were compared at two syncs: - the fully matched run's 11th sync, at learning rate 0; - a sweep run's 7th sync, after 14 optimizer updates at 1e-6. Each covers layers 0, 17 and 35, all four projections, both TP ranks. The engine's E4M3 weights and E8M0 scales equal TE's quantization of the synced weights. The post-processed kernel layouts hold the same bytes, and the learner's cached FP8 forward weights equal the same quantization: **0 of ~600 MB differ** in every comparison. - **The check would catch a stale sampler.** The updates before the second sync had changed 0.84% of the FP8 bytes (at least 0.6% of every matrix), so a sampler still holding the step-0 weights would have failed every comparison. - **The two quantizers agree.** TE's quantizer and vLLM's own MXFP8 quantizer agree byte for byte on all 252 linear weights of Qwen3-8B (6.95 B elements) and on boundary cases. - **What remains.** With the weights byte-identical, 84% of the BF16-sampler mismatch remains. It most likely comes from activation quantization acting on slightly different inputs and from the two engines' different kernels, not from stored weights. **Across settings.** KL at step 1, where all arms of a setting hold the same weights, and over the last 10 steps: | Setting | BF16/BF16 | FP8-TW/BF16 | MXFP8/BF16 | FP8-BW/FP8-BW | MXFP8/MXFP8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A (vLLM) | 0.00066 → 0.00069 | 0.00859 → 0.01217 | 0.00828 → 0.00864 | | 0.00723 → 0.00693 (gate_up BF16) | | C (SGLang) | 0.00064 (step 1) | 0.00881 (step 1) | | | 0.00681 → 0.00670 (all matched) | | B (vLLM, fp8 KV) | 0.00610 → 0.00882 | 0.00915 → 0.02969 | | | 0.00927 → 0.00878 (gate_up BF16) | | D (MoE, vLLM) | 0.00174 → 0.00177 | 0.00519 → 0.00584 | | 0.00921 → 0.00899 | 0.00446 → 0.00449 (all matched) | - **Shared-grid vs. per-tensor FP8.** Among low-precision pipelines, the shared-grid pipeline is the most consistent in every setting. Its last-10-step KL is 43% (A), 70% (B), 46% (C) and 23% (D) below FP8-TW/BF16. At step 1 the margin is smaller, 16% (A), 23% (C), 14% (D) and none in B, because most of the late margin is the per-tensor recipe's drift: its KL grows 3.1× over B's 32 steps, while MXFP8's stays flat. - **Different grids double the mismatch.** On Blackwell, FP8-BW's learner must use power-of-two block scales while its sampler quantizes with FP32 scales, so the two sides round the same weight differently. Its KL is 2× MXFP8's at step 1, before the runs diverge. - **BF16 floor.** BF16 end to end stays ~10× (A) and 2.5× (D) more consistent. B's fp8 KV cache raises its BF16 floor. #### 2. Speed: when MXFP8 pays off **A cost per micro-batch.** In RL the tokens per step `T` change as responses shorten (they halve over setting A), so per-step and per-token times mislead. Instead, each stage's time is fitted as `t = F + c·T` over the run's steps. For setting A's `update_actor` (steps 4–60, ± standard errors): | Arm | F (s) | c (µs/token) | added cost per micro-batch, Δδ (ms) | break-even m* = Δδ/Δc (tokens per micro-batch) | |---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 | 12.31 ± 0.30 | 26.74 ± 0.69 | | | | FP8-TW | 18.10 ± 0.28 | 14.60 ± 0.66 | 45.3 | 3,726 ± 61 | | MXFP8 | 18.89 ± 0.24 | 15.38 ± 0.56 | 51.5 | **4,527 ± 108** | A single run cannot tell a per-step cost from a per-micro-batch one. Three observations favor per-micro-batch: - the added fixed costs of the old-log-prob and update stages are consistent with a per-micro-batch cost, given their micro-batch counts (a consistency check, not a proof); - on a slower-CPU host the same recipe is a net loss; - the per-micro-batch form predicts held-out setting B, at ~12.2k tokens per micro-batch, better than a per-step form. For MXFP8 it predicts per-token savings of 9.0% (old log-prob) and 15.9% (update), against 9.1% and 11.9% measured; a per-step model predicts 13.2% and 20.9%. The recipe therefore pays off above **m\* ≈ 4.5k tokens per micro-batch** on this model and host. **Controlled sweep.** The same replayed token data runs at every step, and only the micro-batch size changes (update-stage time per step, mean of steps 2–6, ± SE over 5 paired steps). The last two columns predict the difference from setting A's constants: | Micro-batch (tokens) | micro-batches per step | BF16 (s) | MXFP8 (s) | MXFP8 − BF16 (s) | predicted, per-micro-batch cost | predicted, per-step cost | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 seq (1.3k) | 512 | 69.12 | 84.49 | +15.37 ± 0.44 | +18.9 | −0.9 | | 2 seq (2.6k) | 256 | 42.90 | 48.71 | +5.81 ± 0.97 | +5.7 | −0.9 | | 4 seq (5.2k) | 128 | 32.72 | 33.36 | +0.64 ± 0.91 | −0.9 | −0.9 | | 8 seq (10.3k) | 64 | 32.47 | 24.86 | −7.61 ± 1.68 | −4.2 | −0.9 | | 4 seq, half batch (5.2k) | 64 | 17.43 | 16.55 | −0.88 ± 0.75 | −0.5 | +2.8 | - **The difference grows with the number of micro-batches,** as a per-micro-batch cost predicts. Fitted on the sweep alone, the added cost is Δδ = 47.0 ± 4.5 ms per micro-batch (setting A: 51.5). - **There is no per-step part.** The sweep's per-step term is Δa = −0.10 ± 3.21 s. - **The crossing.** It sits near 5k tokens, but the sweep does not pin m\* down by itself (2.8k–7.6k under resampling). - **Caveat at 8 sequences.** BF16 does not speed up from 4 to 8 sequences, so part of MXFP8's lead there is BF16's slowdown. **Where the added time goes.** From Nsight Systems on the update stage, 1-sequence micro-batches, rank 0, per micro-batch: | | BF16 | MXFP8 | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | wall time under the profiler (ms) | 159.3 | 202.6 | **+43.4** | | GPU busy: kernels and copies, merged across streams | 69.6 | 75.5 | +5.9 | | no GPU operation running | 89.7 | 127.1 | +37.4 | | — host had not yet issued the next operation | 68.8 | 99.4 | **+30.6** | | — issued, not yet started (launch latency) | 16.4 | 22.7 | +6.3 | | — issued earlier, waiting on other work | 4.6 | 5.1 | +0.5 | | kernel launches | 4,139 | 5,051 | +912 | | wall time without the profiler (ms) | 135.0 | 165.0 | +30.0 | - **The extra kernels are cheap on the GPU.** MXFP8 launches 912 more kernels per micro-batch. 325 are activation and gradient quantizations, and 576 rearrange block scales into the GEMM's layout: 288 for the cached weights and 288 for tensors all-gathered under sequence parallelism. Their 4.8 ms and the longer NCCL kernels (+5.1 ms) are mostly offset by the FP8 GEMMs (−7.1 ms), so the GPU is busy only 5.9 ms longer. - **The cost is host work between GPU operations.** While the GPU waited, the issuing thread was outside every traced call (CUDA API, TE C++, NCCL), that is, in Python and framework code; synchronizing calls take the same time in both recipes. - **Remedies.** CUDA graphs or a faster host should lower m\*. TE ≥ 2.18 writes the cached weights' scales in the GEMM layout, which removes the 288 weight rearrangements, about 1.8 ms of profiled host time. **End to end.** Changes vs. BF16/BF16 on the same host: | | A: dense, gsm8k | B: dense, DAPO | D: MoE, DAPO | |---|---|---|---| | tokens per update micro-batch | ~3.4k (below m\*) | ~12.2k | dynamic batching, up to 20,480 per GPU | | step time | **+5.1%** | **−6.4%** | **−10.7%** | | `update_actor` | +6.9% | −12.1% | −9.4% | | old log-prob | −4.0% (~6.8k tokens per micro-batch) | −9.3% | −5.3% | | generation | −1.1% per token | −2.7% per token | **−23.8%** | | actor peak memory | +4.7% | +2.2% | +25% (60.0 → 75.0 GiB; FP8-BW: 74.6) | - **Setting A's update stage crosses m\* within one run.** In the first four steps, at 4.9–5.3k tokens per micro-batch, MXFP8 is 2.9% faster than BF16. Over the last ten, at 2.7k, it is 13.6% slower. - **Dense rollout speed.** This was measured only in the controlled runs, with every linear on the grid. The MXFP8 sampler generates 5.3% more tokens/s than the BF16 sampler of the same learner, but two identically configured BF16 samplers differ by 3.1%, so dense MXFP8 rollout shows no clear speed-up at this size. - **SGLang backend.** SGLang 0.5.12's default Triton MXFP8 GEMM makes generation 1.9× slower than BF16. Its FlashInfer CUTLASS backend, usable with weight sync after this PR's refit loader, cuts that to 1.4×. - **Weight-sync cost.** Quantizing at every sync adds ~1 s per step on the dense model (3.2 → 4.2 s in A) and 4 s on MoE including the self-check (3.5 → 7.5 s), 1–2% of a step. TE's quantization of all 252 dense weights takes ~11 ms of GPU time. Most of the added time is restoring parameters to a loadable layout (0.57 s) and re-deriving kernel layouts (0.49 s). - **Memory.** TE keeps FP8 copies next to the BF16 weights; on MoE the FP8-BW recipe costs the same. #### 3. Learning dynamics **Accuracy and reward.** There is no regression the data can resolve: - **A.** Held-out gsm8k accuracy after 60 steps is 0.9393 (MXFP8/MXFP8), 0.9363 (BF16), 0.9356 (MXFP8/BF16) and 0.9249 (FP8-TW). This is not an ordering: the MXFP8 sampler already scores 1.9 points higher on the untrained model, and repeating a configuration on another host moved accuracy by up to 2.0 points. - **B.** Reward, response length and truncation track BF16 (last-10 score 0.135 vs. 0.150). **Entropy** separates the recipes most clearly: - under MXFP8 the policy's entropy stays flat or rises (A −4%, B +4%, C +4%, D +6%); - under BF16 (A −49%) and FP8-TW (B −74%) it decays. The flatter policy is in the weights: the BF16 sampler of the MXFP8 learner sees it too. Step-matched checkpoints from different recipes are therefore not at the same point of training. #### 4. Correctness: what a weight sync must preserve After every sync the sampler must: - **C1** quantize exactly the learner's low-precision layers; - **C2** hold the learner's weight grid; - **C3** rebuild every kernel-specific derived layout; - **C4** update the storage CUDA graphs captured; - **C5** finish a streamed update completely; - **C6** produce finite probabilities and bounded divergence; - **C7** report every check's verdict. Each failure found on B200 broke one of these: | | Failure | Breaks | Symptom | Fix / caught now by | |---|---|---|---|---| | F1 | `lm_head` quantized in the sampler (silent) | C1 | NaN logits; reward 0.000 for 20 steps; every response at the length cap | `lm_head` and the embedding are in the default ignore list (#8287; SGLang's `ignored_layers` in this PR); audit, sentinel | | F2 | router exclusion `mlp.gate` also excluded the dense `gate_up_proj` (silent) | C1 | none in the metrics; 56 of 311 parameters flagged on Qwen3-1.7B | not reachable on the compressed-tensors path (anchored `re:.*mlp\.gate$`; on SGLang, whole module-path components); audit's engine re-check | | F3 | stale swizzled scales after sync, SGLang FlashInfer CUTLASS (silent) | C3 | held-out accuracy 0.000; KL 7.2 | refit loader re-runs post-processing (this PR); self-check, sentinel | | F4 | stale MoE expert layout after sync, vLLM TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE (silent) | C3 | expert probe error 1.74 (healthy 0.05); KL 0.047 | record same-shape repacks (#7986); self-check MoE probe | | F5 | BF16 MoE sync crashes on SM100 | C3 | crash at the first sync | in-place staging (#7987) | | F6 | FP32 block scales on SM100 | C2 | assertion at the first FP8 quantization | FP32 scales documented Hopper-only (#8062) | | F7 | guards ran but printed nothing (silent) | C7 | audit produced no output | dedicated log handler, forwarded level, warning when a check cannot run (this PR) | | F8 | MoE layers kept in BF16 by `ignore` under a quantized rollout | C3 | vLLM TRT-LLM: shape error at the first sync (CUTLASS would swap gate and up silently; CPU test only); SGLang MXFP8: crash at the first sync | vLLM: the quantized refit stages and re-derives them (this PR); SGLang: refused before the first sync (this PR) | **The guards are complementary.** Of the four silent faults that reached a run: - only the audit's query of the live engine caught F2; its configured-rule half saw 28 of 28 layers agree; - only the self-check caught F4; - the sentinel fired on F1 (NaN) and F3 (KL 7.2) but stayed silent on F2 (KL 0.007–0.010) and F4 (KL 0.047), so divergence alarms cannot replace mechanism checks. **Healthy runs.** - The self-check read 0.026–0.027 (dense) and 0.049–0.052 (MoE expert), against its 0.25 tolerance; F4 read 1.739. - The audit agreed with the engine on all 69 and 18,867 parameters it checked. - The only false alarm was on the FP8-blockwise path, which has no engine query. #### Before enabling - **Size micro-batches well above m\*** (~4.5k tokens per micro-batch for Qwen3-8B, TP2, fast host): use dynamic batching with a large token budget. Do not benchmark FP8 RL at small micro-batches, and compare timings only on one host. - **Expect more memory**, from TE's FP8 copies. - **Keep importance-sampling correction on.** Matching lowers the systematic offset (KL, log-perplexity) more than the per-token spread: the dual-clip rate is similar for the matched and unmatched MXFP8 arms, about a third of FP8-TW's. - **On SGLang < 0.5.18, set `fp8_gemm_runner_backend=flashinfer_cutlass`.** The default Triton MXFP8 GEMM decodes ~2× slower than BF16. - **On SGLang, do not set `fp8_gemm_runner_backend=deep_gemm` on Blackwell.** Known limitation, not fixed here; a TODO in `mxfp8_refit_loader.py` records the fix. - A dense layer DeepGEMM cannot serve (N % 64 ≠ 0 or K % 128 ≠ 0) falls back to FlashInfer. At every sync SGLang 0.5.20 rebuilds that layer's FlashInfer scale into new storage, while the CUDA graphs captured at startup keep reading the old one, so decode would use a stale scale for that layer. - The post-sync self-check runs the layer eagerly and does not see it. Found by reading SGLang's code, not reproduced on hardware. - The default Blackwell backends (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL / CUTLASS) rebuild their scale in place and are not affected. - **On Blackwell, prefer MXFP8 to FP8-blockwise,** which needs power-of-two scales there (#8062). - **Watch `actor/entropy`** when switching recipes. #### What this does not show - **This version on hardware.** Every B200 result here predates the rebase on #8287 (vLLM then ran the ModelOpt path); re-validation is pending. - **Short runs.** One seed per configuration and 3–60 steps; no claim about final quality. - **The matching experiment.** It runs only at the initial checkpoint and does not split the gain between weights, activations and kernels. - **FP8 KV cache in setting B.** All three arms of B ran vLLM with `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` to shorten generation at 8192-token responses; A, C, D and the controlled runs keep the KV cache in BF16. - It is not MXFP8: K and V are stored as FP8 E4M3 with one scale per tensor (1.0), and on B200 vLLM 0.24 also quantizes Q to FP8 by default. - The learner has no KV cache and computes attention in BF16, so every sampler in B carries a quantization source the learner lacks, whatever its weights. - Comparisons within B stand, but B's absolute KL is not comparable with the other settings, and its BF16 arm is not BF16 end to end: step-1 KL 0.00610 vs. 0.00066 in A, a gap that B's data and response lengths also feed. The cache's share was not measured; switching only `kv_cache_dtype` at fixed weights would measure it. - **The byte check.** It covers 3 of 36 layers at two syncs, dense only, with TE's quantizer on the sync (before the rebase). - **The break-even model.** It rests on one model and one host type. The profile covers one rank and one micro-batch size, and does not name the Python functions that carry the host time. - **MoE.** One model family, vLLM only, 10 steps; the FP8-blockwise path has no self-check. - **Fault injection.** The hardware campaign has not been run; CPU fault-injection tests are in `tests/utils`. ### Reproducing The arms of a setting differ only in their precision flags; model, data, seed, batch sizes, parallelism and learning rate are identical. | Arm | Flags added to the BF16 command line | |---|---| | FP8-TW / BF16 | `++actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.fp8="e4m3"` `++…fp8_recipe="tensorwise"` | | MXFP8 / BF16 | `++…fp8="e4m3"` `++…fp8_recipe="mxfp8"` | | MXFP8 / MXFP8 | `++…fp8="e4m3"` `++…fp8_recipe="mxfp8"` `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.linear=MXFP8` `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization.moe=MXFP8` (the runs used the pre-#8287 `rollout.quantization=mxfp8`) |
Setting A, BF16 arm: command line as resolved at runtime ```bash python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo --config-path=config --config-name=ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml \ data.train_files=/workspace/data/gsm8k/train.parquet \ data.val_files=/workspace/data/gsm8k/test.parquet \ data.return_raw_chat=True \ data.train_batch_size=64 \ data.max_prompt_length=1024 \ data.max_response_length=2048 \ data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \ data.truncation=error \ algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \ algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \ actor_rollout_ref.model.path=/workspace/models/Qwen3-8B \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=32 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size=2 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size=1 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_mbridge=True \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.param_offload=False \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.optimizer_offload=False \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.vanilla_mbridge=False \ ++actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.gradient_accumulation_fusion=False \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=8 \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.tensor_model_parallel_size=2 \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.pipeline_model_parallel_size=1 \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.use_mbridge=True \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.param_offload=False \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.vanilla_mbridge=False \ ++actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.override_transformer_config.gradient_accumulation_fusion=False \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode=async \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=2 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.25 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=8 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.calculate_log_probs=True \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=8 \ trainer.critic_warmup=0 \ 'trainer.logger=["console","tensorboard","file"]' \ trainer.project_name=b200_mxfp8 \ trainer.experiment_name=v3_nooff_bf16 \ trainer.n_gpus_per_node=2 \ trainer.nnodes=1 \ trainer.save_freq=-1 \ trainer.test_freq=999 \ trainer.total_epochs=100 \ trainer.total_training_steps=60 ```
How the other settings differ from A: - **B** uses DAPO-Math-17k, an 8192-token response cap, dynamic batching at 12,288 tokens per GPU, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` in every arm, and 32 steps. - **C** is A with `rollout.name=sglang` on SGLang 0.5.12, 30 steps. - **D** is Qwen3-30B-A3B on 4×B200 (TP2 × EP2), with dynamic batching at 20,480 tokens per GPU, parameter offload, a CPU optimizer, full recompute, FlashInfer autotuning off, and 10 steps. The controlled runs use A's command line with experiment-only hooks that time, log and dump data without changing the computation. ### API and Usage Example No API change; the mode is enabled through existing config: ```yaml # Training: Blackwell (SM100+), Megatron-Core >= 0.13, TE >= 2.1, Megatron-Bridge model path (default) actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config: fp8: "e4m3" # or "hybrid" fp8_recipe: "mxfp8" # 32-element block scaling # Rollout: vLLM (compressed-tensors MXFP8, #8287) or SGLang (its native MXFP8 method) actor_rollout_ref.rollout: name: vllm # or sglang quantization: linear: MXFP8 moe: MXFP8 ``` Weights stay BF16 in training (`fp8_param` is not supported), so checkpoints are unchanged; the sampler starts from the BF16 checkpoint and receives freshly quantized weights after every optimizer step. Guard switches, all read at call time: | Variable | Default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK` | on | `0` disables the post-sync self-check | | `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL`, `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL` | 0.25 | self-check tolerances | | `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT` | `warn` | `raise` makes mismatches fatal; `0` disables the audit | | `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL` | on | `0` disables the step sentinel | | `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX`, `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS` | 1.0, 2 | sentinel thresholds | ### Design & Code Changes **Training** - `verl/models/mcore/util.py`: - `_compute_fp8_thd_align_size` aligns each sequence to `lcm(32, align)` under MXFP8 (via mcore's `get_fp8_align_size`); blockwise is unchanged; - `get_fp8_padding_options` replaces five copies of the padding decision. - `model_forward.py`, `model_forward_fused.py`, `router_replay_utils.py`: pass `fp8_recipe` to every THD preprocess call. - `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: rejects QAT combined with a TE FP8 recipe, since the two contracts conflict. **Export (trainer side)** - #8287's compressed-tensors exporter, unchanged for vLLM. - `verl/utils/qat/compressed_tensors.py`: an SGLang branch in `dispatch_rollout_weight_quantizer` (below). **vLLM rollout** (on #8287's compressed-tensors path) - `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_mxfp8_refit_check.py`, `vllm_quant_utils.py`: the post-sync self-check on `CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8` linear layers and `CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod` experts. The canonical tensors are copied before the staged layers are re-processed. - `utils.py`, `vllm_rollout.py`: `quant_layer_audit_methods` / `quant_methods_of`, through which the audit asks the live engine which quant method each receiving module runs. **SGLang rollout** (its native MXFP8 method) - `sglang_mxfp8_utils.py`: - preset detection and refusals; - the native `quantization_config` (whose `ignored_layers` mirror the exporter's default ignore list on module-path components); - the support check; - `SGLangMxfp8WeightQuantizer`, which emits `weight_scale_inv`. - `async_sglang_server.py`, `sglang_rollout.py`: - native launch with `--quantization mxfp8` and the loader registered; - `load_format` on every bucket plus a closing request; - refusing the delta checkpoint engine with rollout quantization. - `mxfp8_refit_loader.py`: - re-derives the kernel layouts once per sync for every MXFP8 layer whose resolved backend keeps derived scale copies (F3); - stages and folds back MoE expert scales; - checks unwritten scales and the sync-vs-engine dtypes. - `flashinfer_trtllm` (dense) is rejected because it shuffles weights in place. **Guards** - `verl/utils/mxfp8_refit_check.py`: the post-sync self-check core, for the dense probe and the MoE expert probe. - `verl/utils/quant_layer_audit.py`, armed in `engine_workers.py` when training runs a TE FP8 recipe and the rollout is quantized, and hooked on the engine's weight export after the rollout weight quantizer, so every sync route passes through it. It compares: - the learner's FP8 layers with the format of each exported weight; - on vLLM, the export with the live engine's quant methods. - `verl/utils/quant_sentinel.py`, called from `ray_trainer.py` and `v1/trainer_base.py`; armed by the effective rollout quantization. **Where quantization happens during a sync.** Since #8287, both engines receive weights already quantized on the trainer side: `get_per_tensor_param` applies the rollout weight quantizer to the exported HF weights. - **Megatron → SGLang:** `SGLangMxfp8WeightQuantizer` streams `(weight, weight_scale_inv)`; the refit loader re-derives the kernel layouts on the closing request. - **Megatron → vLLM:** the compressed-tensors exporter streams `(weight, weight_scale)`; #8287's refit cycle re-derives the kernel layouts. The figure shows the path before the rebase, when the vLLM worker received BF16 weights and quantized them itself. **Which layers stay in high precision** | Component | Training | vLLM rollout | SGLang rollout | |---|---|---|---| | decoder linears (attention, MLP, MoE experts) | MXFP8 GEMMs (fprop, dgrad, wgrad) | MXFP8, quantized at each sync by the trainer's compressed-tensors exporter | same | | `lm_head`, token embedding | BF16 (not TE FP8 linears) | BF16: compressed-tensors' default ignore list | BF16: `ignored_layers` (the same default list) | | MoE router, shared-expert gate | BF16/FP32, outside FP8 GEMMs | BF16: default ignore list (`re:.*mlp\.gate$`, `re:.*shared_expert_gate$`) | BF16: `ignored_layers` (`mlp.gate`, `shared_expert_gate`) | | attention, norms, sampling | BF16 / FP32 | BF16 (KV cache BF16 unless `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`) | same | **Docs and tests** - `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`: - "MXFP8 Training (Blackwell)", covering how the exporter's scales compare with TE's; - "MXFP8 Rollout on SGLang"; - "Post-sync self-check"; - "Quantized-layer audit"; - the sentinel section. - Eight new CPU test files, listed under **Test**. ### AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance, including the code, the B200 experiment design, the measurement methodology and analysis in the validation section, and the figures. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, commissioned and reviewed the B200 runs, and can defend the design end to end, including: - why MXFP8 needs 32-token alignment in training (TE's columnwise wgrad layout) but not at inference; - why putting the sampler on the learner's weight grid removes the weight part of the train–inference mismatch but not the activation part; - how the refit cycle keeps CUDA-graph-captured storage stable across per-step weight updates. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting). - [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/low_precision/fp8.md`. - [x] Add unit test(s): eight CPU test files (see **Test**); Blackwell end-to-end runs in **B200 validation**. - [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 # FP8 RL in verl
 
-Last updated: 09/29/2026
+Last updated: 10/20/2026
 
 verl supports two FP8 modes for accelerating RL training:
 
@@ -122,6 +122,23 @@ Results and observations:
 - FP8 rollout : over 35% rollout speedup
 - Expecting more perf gain with CUDA 12.9
 
+### Quantized-rollout sentinel
+
+When the rollout is quantized, both trainers check each step's metrics for the signs of a broken
+rollout:
+
+- `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` is non-finite while the batch had valid tokens;
+- `rollout_corr/kl` is non-finite or above 1.0 (healthy quantized rollouts read about 0.001–0.03);
+- every response hits the length cap (`response_length/clip_ratio` close to 1) on two consecutive steps.
+  This rule is off under `rollout.ignore_eos`, where every response runs to the cap by design.
+
+`VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL=warn` (the default) logs a finding with its likely causes and lets the run go on;
+`=raise` stops the run instead; `=0` disables the check. `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_KL_MAX` sets the KL bound
+and `VERL_QUANT_SENTINEL_CLIP_STEPS` the number of steps (`0` turns the length-cap rule off). The rollout
+counts as quantized when `rollout.quantization` sets `linear`, `moe` or `config_file`, or the model's own
+`config.json` (local paths only) carries a `quantization_config`. The sentinel catches gross failures
+only: one layer type left unquantized (KL 0.007–0.010) stays within the healthy range.
+
 ---
 
 ## FP8 End-to-End (Training + Rollout)
@@ -180,6 +197,119 @@ Results and observations:
 
 ---
 
+## MXFP8 Training (Blackwell)
+
+MXFP8 is the OCP microscaling FP8 format: E4M3 elements with one E8M0 scale per 32-element block,
+decoded natively by Blackwell tensor cores. On Hopper, use the `blockwise` recipe above.
+
+### Requirements
+
+- Blackwell GPUs (SM100+)
+- Megatron-Core >= 0.13 and Transformer Engine >= 2.1
+
+### Key Configuration
+
+```yaml
+# MXFP8 training via Transformer Engine
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config:
+  fp8: "e4m3"                # element format; "hybrid" (e4m3 fwd + e5m2 bwd) also supported
+  fp8_recipe: "mxfp8"        # 32-element block scaling
+
+# MXFP8 rollout (vLLM)
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.quantization:
+  linear: MXFP8
+  moe: MXFP8
+```
+
+Notes:
+
+- Weights stay in BF16 (`fp8_param` is not supported); only the GEMM inputs are cast to MXFP8, so
+  checkpoints are unchanged.
+- With `fp8_recipe: "mxfp8"`, verl pads packed sequences to the 32-token blocks MXFP8 needs.
+- QAT and Transformer Engine FP8 training are mutually exclusive; the engine refuses the combination.
+- The rollout's MXFP8 weights are quantized on the trainer side (the compressed-tensors exporter of
+  `rollout.quantization`). Given the same BF16 weight, compressed-tensors and Transformer Engine pick the
+  same E8M0 scale for every block except those whose amax is exactly `448 * 2**k`, where compressed-tensors
+  picks the next one up; in such a block only elements below `amax / 14336` dequantize differently, by at
+  most about `4.4e-6 * amax`. This compares the weight quantizers only, not activations, reduction order or
+  the KV cache.
+- `lm_head`, the token embedding and MoE routers stay in BF16 on the rollout, as in training.
+
+### MXFP8 Rollout on SGLang
+
+```yaml
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout:
+  name: sglang
+  quantization:
+    linear: MXFP8
+    moe: MXFP8
+```
+
+SGLang serves this preset with its own MXFP8 method (`quant_method: mxfp8`): verl translates the
+configuration, exports the scales under SGLang's names and re-derives SGLang's kernel layouts after every
+weight sync; see [Low-Precision Rollout and Quantization-Aware Training](qat.md). verl pins SGLang's MXFP8
+dense and MoE kernels to DeepGEMM; `VERL_ROLLOUT_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` leaves the choice to SGLang.
+
+Two configurations are refused before anything is written:
+
+- MoE layers kept in BF16 (`rollout.quantization.ignore`) whose experts the MoE runner re-laid out at load:
+  SGLang's FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner stores BF16 experts in a block layout a weight sync cannot write.
+  DeepGEMM keeps them in checkpoint layout.
+- The delta checkpoint engine with any quantized rollout (`rollout.quantization` or the checkpoint's own
+  `quantization_config`): it applies its payloads without the trainer-side weight quantization.
+
+Do not set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` for an SGLang rollout: verl starts SGLang
+with `enable_memory_saver=True`, which refuses that allocator mode.
+
+### Post-sync self-check
+
+After loading, both engines derive kernel-specific copies of the MXFP8 weights and scales (swizzled
+scales, shuffled or packed experts). If a sync skips that step, the kernel pairs fresh weights with stale
+scales while every shape and dtype still matches. After every sync, verl therefore runs the smallest MXFP8
+linear layer and one expert of the smallest MXFP8 MoE layer through their own kernels on a small random
+input and compares the output with a BF16 reference on the dequantized canonical weights. Healthy layers
+read a relative error of about 0.03 (dense) and 0.05 (experts); a stale layout reads O(1).
+
+- `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK=warn` (the default) logs a failed check and lets the sync go on, `=raise` stops
+  the sync, `=0` skips the checks. `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_TOL` (default 0.25) and
+  `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK_MOE_TOL` set the thresholds.
+- On SGLang, the refit loader also reports experts whose scales the sync did not write.
+- The expert probe is skipped, with a warning, where its made-up routing cannot send every row to one
+  expert at weight 1. On vLLM: expert or data parallelism, non-SiLU gates, and, on monolithic MoE kernels, a
+  routed scaling factor, grouped top-k, a score correction bias or custom routing. On SGLang: expert
+  parallelism, TP without `reduce_results`, and non-softmax, grouped, biased or custom routing.
+
+What it does not show:
+
+- It samples one dense layer and one expert per sync; a layer outside the sample can still be stale.
+- It runs the kernels eagerly. A re-derivation into new storage, instead of the storage a CUDA graph
+  captured, passes the probe while graph replays keep reading the old values. That the captured storage is
+  updated rests on indirect evidence (the re-derived layouts are copied back in place, and the KL stays in
+  its healthy range), not on a graph replay.
+
+### Quantized-layer audit
+
+Training decides implicitly which layers run FP8 (TE linear modules inside `fp8_autocast`); the rollout
+decides by name (`rollout.quantization`, read by both the trainer-side exporter and the engine). When
+training runs a TE FP8 recipe and the rollout is quantized, verl compares them at the first weight sync
+after a training step:
+
+- **Training vs export**: each decoder layer's FP8 trace (TE's FP8 weight workspaces) against the format
+  the sync sends for that layer's GEMM projections (attention, MLP, experts, linear-attention and SSM in /
+  out projections). Weights the exporter keeps in BF16 by design are skipped. Other decoder-layer weights,
+  such as a convolution, are not judged, and the audit reports how many it left out.
+- **Export vs engine**: on vLLM, the format of every synced weight against the quant method of the module
+  that receives it. On SGLang, the refit loader compares each incoming weight's dtype with the parameter
+  that receives it before writing it (switched by `VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK`).
+
+`VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT=warn` (the default) logs a disagreement, `=raise` stops the run, `=0` disables the
+audit, and `VERL_QUANT_LAYER_AUDIT_TRACE=1` logs each step of the audit itself. The training-side trace is
+per layer, so a TE module kept in BF16 inside an FP8 layer would go unnoticed (Megatron has no such
+per-module option today). With `disable_parameter_transpose_cache=True` TE keeps no FP8 workspace, and the
+audit warns once that it cannot run.
+
+---
+
 ## Citation
 
 For more extensive experiments, ablation studies, and analysis on FP8 reinforcement learning, please refer to our technical report:

+"""FP8 padding alignment for THD preprocessing, incl. the mxfp8 recipe."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+import verl.utils.device as device_module
+
+
+def _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size: int = 1, cp_size: int = 1, cp_rank: int = 0):
+    megatron = types.ModuleType("megatron")
+    core = types.ModuleType("megatron.core")
+    parallel_state = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.parallel_state")
+    packed_seq_params = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.packed_seq_params")
+
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_world_size = lambda: cp_size
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_rank = lambda: cp_rank
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_group = lambda: object()
+    parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size = lambda: tp_size
+
+    class PackedSeqParams:
+        def __init__(self, **kwargs):
+            self.__dict__.update(kwargs)
+
+    packed_seq_params.PackedSeqParams = PackedSeqParams
+
+    # Mirrors megatron.core.fp8_utils.get_fp8_align_size for CI hosts without megatron.
+    fp8_utils = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.fp8_utils")
+    fp8_utils.get_fp8_align_size = lambda fp8_recipe: 32 if fp8_recipe == "mxfp8" else 16
+
+    core.parallel_state = parallel_state
+    core.fp8_utils = fp8_utils
+    megatron.core = core
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron", megatron)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core", core)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core.parallel_state", parallel_state)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core.packed_seq_params", packed_seq_params)
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "megatron.core.fp8_utils", fp8_utils)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(device_module, "is_npu_available", False)
+
+    util_path = Path(__file__).parents[2] / "verl" / "models" / "mcore" / "util.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("mcore_util_fp8_padding", util_path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+def test_compute_fp8_thd_align_size(monkeypatch):
+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch)
+
+    # Default (blockwise & friends): per-seq lcm(16, align), total align*128.
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(1) == (16, 128)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(2) == (16, 256)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(2, "blockwise") == (16, 256)
+    assert mcore_util._compute_fp8_thd_align_size(12) == (48, 12 * 128)
+
+    # mxfp8 scales in 32-element blocks: per-seq lcm(32, align).

+"""Regression tests: which layers an MXFP8 rollout keeps in BF16.
+
+Both contracts below are the trainer-side exporter's default ignore list, which the
+rollout's compressed-tensors config carries as well; a preset or a user ``ignore``
+list adds to it and cannot remove it. Both failures were silent on 2xB200:
+
+- Quantizing ``lm_head`` makes the rollout logits ``nan`` (Qwen3-8B / gsm8k: reward
+  0.0 for all 20 steps, every ``rollout_corr/*`` metric ``nan``, exit code 0).
+- vLLM 0.24's ModelOpt MXFP8 config matched the router exclusion ``mlp.gate`` as a
+  prefix of ``mlp.gate_up_proj``, so the dense MLPs were served in BF16 while training
+  ran them in FP8 (56 of 311 parameters of Qwen3-1.7B).
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.qat.compressed_tensors import DEFAULT_IGNORE, _matches
+
+requires_ct = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    importlib.util.find_spec("compressed_tensors") is None, reason="compressed-tensors is not installed"
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "module", ["lm_head", "model.embed_tokens", "model.language_model.lm_head", "model.language_model.embed_tokens"]
+)
+def test_default_ignore_keeps_lm_head_and_the_embedding(module):
+    assert _matches(module, DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+
+
+def test_default_ignore_keeps_routers_but_not_gate_up_proj():
+    # The router (mlp.gate) and the shared-expert gate stay in BF16; the gated MLP projections do not.
+    assert _matches("model.layers.0.mlp.gate", DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+    assert _matches("model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert_gate", DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+    assert not _matches("model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj", DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+    assert not _matches("model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj", DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+    assert not _matches("model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert.gate_proj", DEFAULT_IGNORE)
+
+
+@requires_ct
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("linear", "moe"), [("MXFP8", "MXFP8"), ("MXFP8", None)])
+def test_mxfp8_export_leaves_lm_head_and_the_embedding_in_bf16(linear, moe):
+    from verl.utils.qat.compressed_tensors import CompressedTensorsWeightQuantizer, build_compressed_tensors_config
+
+    config = build_compressed_tensors_config(linear=linear, moe=moe, ignore=[r"re:.*layers\.0\..*"], config_file=None)
+    assert config["ignore"][: len(DEFAULT_IGNORE)] == DEFAULT_IGNORE  # the user list is added, not substituted
+    weights = [
+        ("lm_head.weight", torch.randn(256, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)),
+        ("model.embed_tokens.weight", torch.randn(256, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)),
+    ]
+    out = dict(CompressedTensorsWeightQuantizer(config)(weights))
+    assert set(out) == {"lm_head.weight", "model.embed_tokens.weight"}
+    assert all(tensor.dtype == torch.bfloat16 for tensor in out.values())

+def test_dequantize_applies_per_block_power_of_two():

+    w = mxfp8_dequantize(q, scale)
+    assert torch.equal(w[0, :32], torch.ones(32)) and torch.equal(w[0, 32:], torch.full((32,), 2.0))
+    assert torch.equal(w[1, :32], torch.full((32,), 0.5)) and torch.equal(w[1, 32:], torch.full((32,), 8.0))

+    w = mxfp8_dequantize(q, scale)

+"""CPU tests for the train/rollout quantized-layer audit (Megatron and vLLM modules faked)."""

+import logging
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.quant_layer_audit import (
+    FP8_WORKSPACE_SEEN_ATTR,
+    QuantLayerAuditor,
+    audit_train_vs_export,
+    collect_train_fp8_report,
+    exported_weight,
+    fp8_recipe_of,
+    merge_worker_methods,
+    remember_fp8_workspaces,
+    trace,
+    unjudged_weights,
+    vllm_quant_methods,
+)
+
+N_LAYERS = 4
+_AUDIT_LOGGER = "verl.utils.quant_layer_audit"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _audit_logs_reach_caplog(caplog):
+    # The audit logger does not propagate (it writes to stderr on its own); attach caplog's handler to it.
+    log = logging.getLogger(_AUDIT_LOGGER)
+    log.addHandler(caplog.handler)
+    level = log.level
+    log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
+    yield
+    log.setLevel(level)
+    log.removeHandler(caplog.handler)
+
+
+class _TELinear(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A TE linear as it looks after the first FP8 forward: it holds a weight workspace."""
+
+    def __init__(self, quantized: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(4, 64), requires_grad=False)
+        if quantized:
+            self._fp8_workspaces = {"weight": object()}
+
+
+class TransformerLayer(torch.nn.Module):  # name matters: the audit looks for *TransformerLayer*
+    def __init__(self, layer_number: int, quantized: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layer_number = layer_number  # mcore: 1-based, global across PP
+        self.self_attention = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.self_attention.linear_qkv = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.self_attention.linear_proj = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.mlp = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.mlp.linear_fc1 = _TELinear(quantized)
+        self.mlp.linear_fc2 = _TELinear(quantized)
+
+
+class _Chunk(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, quantized_layers, n=N_LAYERS):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.embedding = torch.nn.Embedding(10, 4)
+        self.decoder = torch.nn.Module()
+        self.decoder.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([TransformerLayer(i + 1, i in quantized_layers) for i in range(n)])
+        self.output_layer = torch.nn.Linear(4, 10)  # mcore ColumnParallelLinear: never TE

+def _hf_names(n=N_LAYERS, router=None, experts=None):
+    """Qwen/Llama-style dense names; ``router`` adds a router weight per layer, ``experts`` a
+    (prefix, [leaf names]) pair adding two experts per layer, e.g. ("block_sparse_moe.experts", ["w1", "w2", "w3"])."""
+    names = ["model.embed_tokens.weight", "model.norm.weight", "lm_head.weight"]
+    for i in range(n):
+        p = f"model.layers.{i}."
+        names += [
+            p + "self_attn.q_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.k_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.v_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.o_proj.weight",
+            p + "self_attn.q_norm.weight",
+            p + "mlp.gate_proj.weight",
+            p + "mlp.up_proj.weight",
+            p + "mlp.down_proj.weight",
+            p + "input_layernorm.weight",
+            p + "post_attention_layernorm.weight",
+        ]
+        if router:
+            names.append(p + router)
+        if experts:
+            prefix, leaves = experts
+            for e in range(2):
+                names += [f"{p}{prefix}.{e}.{leaf}.weight" for leaf in leaves]
+    return names
+
+
+def _preset_quantizes(name):
+    """What the MXFP8 preset with no extra ``ignore`` sends quantized: the projections and the experts."""
+    return name.endswith("_proj.weight") or ".experts." in name
+
+
+def _export(names, quantizes=_preset_quantizes):
+    """The weight stream after the rollout quantizer: an FP8 weight plus its scale, or the BF16 weight."""
+    stream = []
+    for name in names:
+        if quantizes(name):
+            stream.append((name, torch.zeros(4, 64, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)))
+            stream.append((name + "_scale", torch.zeros(4, 2, dtype=torch.uint8)))
+        else:
+            stream.append((name, torch.zeros(4, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)))
+    return stream
+
+
+def _recorded(names, quantizes=_preset_quantizes):
+    auditor = QuantLayerAuditor("warn")
+    list(auditor.record(iter(_export(names, quantizes))))
+    return auditor.exported
+
+
+def _problem_names(problems):
+    return {p.split(":")[0] for p in problems}
+

+class CompressedTensorsLinearMethod:
+    pass
+
+
+class UnquantizedLinearMethod:
+    pass
+
+
+class UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod:
+    pass
+
+
+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8:
+    pass
+
+
+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod:
+    pass
+
+
+class PPMissingLayer(torch.nn.Module):
+    pass
+
+
+def _vllm_linear(quantized=True):
+    module = torch.nn.Module()
+    if quantized:
+        module.quant_method = CompressedTensorsLinearMethod()
+        module.scheme = CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8()
+    else:
+        module.quant_method = UnquantizedLinearMethod()
+    return module
+
+
+def _vllm_model():
+    """A vLLM-shaped Qwen-MoE-ish model: fused qkv / gate_up, a MoE runner, a LoRA wrapper, a PP stub."""
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.packed_modules_mapping = {
+        "qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"],
+        "gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"],
+    }
+    model.model = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.self_attn = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.self_attn.qkv_proj = _vllm_linear()
+    lora = torch.nn.Module()
+    lora.base_layer = _vllm_linear()
+    layer.self_attn.o_proj = lora
+    layer.mlp = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.mlp.gate = _vllm_linear(quantized=False)
+    layer.mlp.gate_up_proj = _vllm_linear()
+    runner = torch.nn.Module()
+    runner.routed_experts = torch.nn.Module()
+    runner.routed_experts.w13_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1), requires_grad=False)
+    runner.routed_experts.quant_method = CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod()
+    layer.mlp.experts = runner
+    model.model.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([layer, PPMissingLayer()])
+    model.lm_head = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.lm_head.quant_method = UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
+    model.model.norm = torch.nn.Module()  # no quant_method at all
+    return model
+

+"""CPU tests for the SGLang quantized refit loader on MXFP8 layers (sglang stubbed)."""
+
+import enum
+import logging
+import sys
+import types
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Callable, NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check import mxfp8_dequantize
+from verl.utils.sglang import sglang_fp8_utils as fp8_utils
+from verl.utils.sglang import sglang_mxfp8_refit_check as refit_check
+from verl.utils.sglang import sglang_quant_utils as quant_utils
+
+
+class _Backend:
+    def __init__(self, name):
+        self.name = name
+
+    def is_flashinfer_trtllm(self):
+        return self.name == "flashinfer_trtllm"
+
+    def is_flashinfer_cutlass(self):
+        return self.name == "flashinfer_cutlass"
+
+    def is_flashinfer_cutedsl(self):
+        return self.name == "flashinfer_cutedsl"
+
+    def is_deep_gemm(self):
+        return self.name == "deep_gemm"
+
+
+class _StandardTopKOutput(NamedTuple):  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk.StandardTopKOutput
+    topk_weights: torch.Tensor
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor
+    router_logits: torch.Tensor
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _TopKConfig:  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk.TopKConfig (the fields the probe reads)
+    top_k: int
+    use_grouped_topk: bool = False
+    renormalize: bool = True
+    num_fused_shared_experts: int = 0
+    custom_routing_function: Optional[Callable] = None
+    correction_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    routed_scaling_factor: Optional[float] = None
+    scoring_func: str = "softmax"
+
+
+class _BypassedTopKOutput(NamedTuple):  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk.BypassedTopKOutput
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor
+    router_logits: torch.Tensor
+    topk_config: _TopKConfig
+
+
+class _RoutingMethodType(enum.IntEnum):  # sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils.RoutingMethodType
+    Default = 0
+    Renormalize = 1
+    DeepSeekV3 = 2
+    Llama4 = 3
+    RenormalizeNaive = 4
+    TopK = 5
+
+
+class _TopK(torch.nn.Module):
+    """sglang ``TopK.forward_cuda``: the router logits themselves for FlashInfer TRT-LLM, a softmax top-k otherwise."""
+
+    def __init__(self, top_k=2, runner="standard", **cfg):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.topk_config = _TopKConfig(top_k=top_k, **cfg)
+        self.runner = runner
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states, router_logits):
+        if self.runner == "trtllm":
+            return _BypassedTopKOutput(hidden_states, router_logits, self.topk_config)
+        top = torch.softmax(router_logits.float(), dim=-1).topk(self.topk_config.top_k, dim=-1)
+        weights = top.values / top.values.sum(-1, keepdim=True) if self.topk_config.renormalize else top.values
+        return _StandardTopKOutput(weights, top.indices.to(torch.int32), router_logits)
+
+
+# The sglang stubs are installed through the running test's monkeypatch, so they are removed again when the
+# test ends instead of leaking into later tests in the same process.
+_STUB_PATCHES: list = []
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _undo_sglang_stubs(monkeypatch):
+    _STUB_PATCHES.append(monkeypatch)
+    # The self-check tests exercise the failure path; the default mode (warn) has its own tests.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK", "raise")
+    yield
+    _STUB_PATCHES.pop()
+
+
+def _set_module(name, module):
+    _STUB_PATCHES[-1].setitem(sys.modules, name, module)
+
+
+def _install_stub(backend_name):
+    mod = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils")
+    mod.get_fp8_gemm_runner_backend = lambda: _Backend(backend_name)
+    for name in (
+        "sglang",
+        "sglang.srt",
+        "sglang.srt.layers",
+        "sglang.srt.layers.quantization",
+        "sglang.srt.layers.moe",
+    ):
+        if name not in sys.modules:
+            _set_module(name, types.ModuleType(name))
+    _set_module("sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils", mod)
+    topk = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk")
+    topk.StandardTopKOutput = _StandardTopKOutput
+    topk.BypassedTopKOutput = _BypassedTopKOutput
+    topk.TopK = _TopK
+    _set_module("sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk", topk)
+    utils = types.ModuleType("sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils")
+    utils.RoutingMethodType = _RoutingMethodType
+    _set_module("sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils", utils)
+
+
+class _QuantMethod:
+    use_mxfp8 = True
+    is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized = True
+
+    def __init__(self, resolved_backend=None):
+        self.calls = 0
+        # sglang >= 0.5.18 stores the resolved MXFP8 dense backend on the quant method
+        if resolved_backend is not None:
+            self.mxfp8_dense_backend = _Backend(resolved_backend)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        self.calls += 1
+        layer.weight_scale_inv_swizzled = layer.weight_scale_inv.clone() + 1
+
+    def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+        # A FlashInfer-style kernel reads only the derived copy; "+1" is the fake swizzle.
+        scale = layer.weight_scale_inv_swizzled - 1
+        return (x.float() @ mxfp8_dequantize(layer.weight.data, scale).t()).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+class _Linear(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, resolved_backend=None):
+        super().__init__()
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.randint(-6, 7, (4, 64), generator=g).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.full((4, 2), 127, dtype=torch.uint8), requires_grad=False)
+        self.quant_method = _QuantMethod(resolved_backend)
+        self.weight_scale_inv_swizzled = self.weight_scale_inv.clone() + 1  # as after the initial load
+
+
+class _MoEQuantMethod:
+    """sglang ``Fp8MoEMethod`` with an fp8-serialized MXFP8 checkpoint on the CUTLASS MoE runner of sglang >= 0.5.16:
+    post-load processing swizzles the expert scales *in place* into a different shape."""
+
+    use_mxfp8 = True
+    is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized = True
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls = 0
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        self.calls += 1
+        # the copy the kernel reads is derived from the canonical scales present at this moment
+        layer._kernel_scales = (layer.w13_weight_scale_inv.data.clone(), layer.w2_weight_scale_inv.data.clone())
+        for name in ("w13_weight_scale_inv", "w2_weight_scale_inv"):
+            p = getattr(layer, name)
+            swizzled = p.data.reshape(p.data.shape[0], -1).clone() + 1
+            if p.data.shape == swizzled.shape:
+                p.data.copy_(swizzled)
+            else:
+                p.data = swizzled  # sglang's _copy_or_rebind on shape change
+
+
+class _MoE(torch.nn.Module):
+    """sglang ``FusedMoE`` stand-in. ``runner="trtllm"`` behaves like the FlashInfer TRT-LLM runner: w13 is stored as
+    ``[up; gate]`` and the layer only accepts the router logits (it routes inside the kernel: top-k, then softmax)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, experts=2, inter=64, hidden=64, random=False, runner="standard"):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.runner = runner
+        self.use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe = runner == "trtllm"
+        self.routing_method_type = _RoutingMethodType.Renormalize if runner == "trtllm" else None
+        self.moe_runner_config = types.SimpleNamespace(routed_scaling_factor=None)
+        self.formats_seen = []
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+        w13 = (
+            torch.randint(-6, 7, (experts, 2 * inter, hidden), generator=g)
+            if random
+            else torch.zeros(experts, 2 * inter, hidden)
+        )
+        w2 = (
+            torch.randint(-6, 7, (experts, hidden, inter), generator=g)
+            if random
+            else torch.zeros(experts, hidden, inter)
+        )
+        self.w13_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w13.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False)
+        self.w2_weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w2.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False)
+        self.moe_ep_size = 1
+        self.moe_tp_size = 1
+        self.reduce_results = False
+        self.num_experts = experts
+        self.w13_weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.full((experts, 2 * inter, hidden // 32), 127, dtype=torch.uint8), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.w2_weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.full((experts, hidden, inter // 32), 127, dtype=torch.uint8), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.quant_method = _MoEQuantMethod()
+
+    def forward(self, x, topk_output):
+        """sglang FusedMoE.forward stand-in: routed sum of gated-MLP experts on the scales the kernel reads."""
+        from verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check import mxfp8_moe_expert_reference
+
+        if self.runner == "trtllm":
+            assert isinstance(topk_output, _BypassedTopKOutput)  # flashinfer_trtllm.py: a bare assert in sglang
+            top = topk_output.router_logits.float().topk(topk_output.topk_config.top_k, dim=-1)
+            ids, weights = top.indices, torch.softmax(top.values, dim=-1)
+        else:
+            assert isinstance(topk_output, _StandardTopKOutput)
+            ids, weights = topk_output.topk_ids, topk_output.topk_weights
+        self.formats_seen.append(type(topk_output).__name__)
+        s13, s2 = self._kernel_scales
+        out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], self.w2_weight.shape[1])
+        for j in range(ids.shape[1]):
+            for e in ids[:, j].unique().tolist():
+                rows = ids[:, j] == e
+                y = mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(
+                    x[rows],
+                    self.w13_weight.data[e],
+                    s13[e],
+                    self.w2_weight.data[e],
+                    s2[e],
+                    up_first=self.runner == "trtllm",
+                )
+                out[rows] += weights[rows, j : j + 1].float() * y
+        return out.to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+class _Model(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, resolved_backend=None):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.a = _Linear(resolved_backend)
+        self.b = _Linear(resolved_backend)
+        self.plain = torch.nn.Linear(2, 2)  # no quant_method → ignored
+        self.loaded = []
+
+    def load_weights(self, named_tensors):
+        for name, t in named_tensors:
+            self.loaded.append(name)
+            module_name, param = name.rsplit(".", 1)
+            getattr(getattr(self, module_name), param).data.copy_(t)
+
+
+def test_cutlass_backend_reprocesses_every_mxfp8_layer_after_load():
+    _install_stub("flashinfer_cutlass")
+    m = _Model()
+    new_scale = torch.full((4, 2), 7, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    quant_utils.load_and_reprocess(
+        m, [("a.weight_scale_inv", new_scale), ("b.weight_scale_inv", new_scale)] + quant_utils.finalize_tensors()
+    )
+    assert m.loaded == ["a.weight_scale_inv", "b.weight_scale_inv"]
+    assert m.a.quant_method.calls == 1 and m.b.quant_method.calls == 1
+    # swizzled copy derived from the *new* canonical scales
+    assert torch.equal(m.a.weight_scale_inv_swizzled, new_scale + 1)
+
+
+def test_triton_backend_is_a_noop_after_load():
+    _install_stub("triton")
+    m = _Model()
+    n = fp8_utils.reprocess_mxfp8_layers(m)

+def test_trtllm_backend_is_rejected():
+    _install_stub("flashinfer_trtllm")
+    m = _Model()
+    try:
+        fp8_utils.reprocess_mxfp8_layers(m)

+"""The vLLM MXFP8 refit self-check probes compressed-tensors MXFP8 layers and catches a stale kernel copy.
+
+vLLM's compressed-tensors MXFP8 kernels read a copy derived from the canonical weight
+scales when a layer is processed, and leave the parameter itself in a kernel layout. The
+stand-ins below do the same: processing stores the derived copy the kernel reads and
+flattens the parameter, and staging hands the loader a checkpoint-shaped parameter again,
+so a sync whose layers are not re-processed leaves the kernel on the previous scales.
+The modules are loaded by path, so these run without vLLM.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import logging
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check import mxfp8_dequantize, mxfp8_moe_expert_reference
+
+_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+_CORE_LOGGER = "verl.utils.mxfp8_refit_check"
+N, K = 16, 128
+E, INTER, HID = 2, 32, 64
+
+
+def _load_by_path(name, relpath):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, _REPO_ROOT / relpath)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+check = _load_by_path("vllm_mxfp8_refit_check_under_test", "verl/utils/vllm/vllm_mxfp8_refit_check.py")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _check_raises(monkeypatch):
+    # These tests exercise the failure path; the default mode (warn) is tested on its own.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VERL_MXFP8_REFIT_CHECK", "raise")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(check, "_WARNED", set())
+
+
+def _mxfp8(shape, seed):
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    # fp8-representable values: small integers scaled by a per-block power of two
+    q = torch.randint(-6, 7, shape, generator=g).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.randint(124, 130, (*shape[:-1], shape[-1] // 32), generator=g).to(torch.uint8)
+    return q, scale
+
+
+def _param(t):
+    return torch.nn.Parameter(t, requires_grad=False)
+
+
+# The stand-ins carry vLLM's class names: the check selects layers by them.
+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8:
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        layer._kernel_scale = layer.weight_scale.data.clone()
+        layer.weight_scale = _param(layer.weight_scale.data.reshape(-1).clone())
+
+    def apply_weights(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+        return (x.float() @ mxfp8_dequantize(layer.weight.data, layer._kernel_scale).t()).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8(CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8):
+    pass
+
+
+class CompressedTensorsLinearMethod:
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        layer.scheme.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+        return layer.scheme.apply_weights(layer, x, bias=bias)
+
+
+class CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod:
+    is_monolithic = False
+    topk_indices_dtype = None
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        layer._kernel_scales = (layer.w13_weight_scale.data.clone(), layer.w2_weight_scale.data.clone())
+        for name in ("w13_weight_scale", "w2_weight_scale"):
+            setattr(layer, name, _param(getattr(layer, name).data.reshape(E, -1).clone()))
+
+
+def _linear(n=N, scheme=CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8, seed=0):
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    q, scale = _mxfp8((n, K), seed)
+    layer.weight = _param(q)
+    layer.weight_scale = _param(scale)
+    layer.scheme = scheme()
+    layer.quant_method = CompressedTensorsLinearMethod()
+    layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)  # initial load
+    return layer
+
+
+class _RoutedExperts(torch.nn.Module):
+    """vLLM RoutedExperts stand-in: fused expert weights and the modular forward the probe calls."""
+
+    def __init__(self, ep=1, dp=1, activation="silu"):
+        super().__init__()
+        w13, s13 = _mxfp8((E, 2 * INTER, HID), 2)
+        w2, s2 = _mxfp8((E, HID, INTER), 3)
+        self.w13_weight, self.w13_weight_scale = _param(w13), _param(s13)
+        self.w2_weight, self.w2_weight_scale = _param(w2), _param(s2)
+        parallel = SimpleNamespace(tp_size=1, ep_size=ep, dp_size=dp, use_ep=ep > 1)
+        self.moe_config = SimpleNamespace(moe_parallel_config=parallel)
+        self.top_k = 2
+        self.activation = activation
+        self.quant_method = CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod()
+        self.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(self)  # initial load
+
+    def forward_modular(self, x, topk_weights, topk_ids):
+        s13, s2 = self._kernel_scales
+        out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], HID)
+        for r in range(x.shape[0]):
+            for j in range(topk_ids.shape[1]):
+                weight, e = float(topk_weights[r, j]), int(topk_ids[r, j])
+                if weight:
+                    w13, w2 = self.w13_weight.data[e], self.w2_weight.data[e]
+                    out[r] += weight * mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(x[r : r + 1], w13, s13[e], w2, s2[e])[0]
+        return out.to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _stage(model):
+    """The refit staging: give the loader checkpoint-shaped parameters again; returns the staged layers."""
+    staged = []
+    for module in model.modules():
+        if isinstance(getattr(module, "quant_method", None), CompressedTensorsLinearMethod):
+            n, k = module.weight.shape
+            module.weight_scale = _param(module.weight_scale.data.reshape(n, k // 32).clone())
+        elif isinstance(getattr(module, "quant_method", None), CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod):
+            module.w13_weight_scale = _param(module.w13_weight_scale.data.reshape(E, 2 * INTER, HID // 32).clone())
+            module.w2_weight_scale = _param(module.w2_weight_scale.data.reshape(E, HID, INTER // 32).clone())
+        else:
+            continue
+        staged.append(module)
+    return staged
+
+
+def _reprocess(layers):
+    for layer in layers:
+        layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+
+def _sync(model, delta):
+    """A weight sync writing new canonical scales (each step of ``delta`` doubles the weights)."""
+    for module in model.modules():
+        for name in ("weight_scale", "w13_weight_scale", "w2_weight_scale"):
+            if isinstance(getattr(module, name, None), torch.Tensor):
+                getattr(module, name).data.add_(delta)
+

+def _monolithic_experts(**routing):
+    """RoutedExperts on a monolithic kernel that, like vLLM's, routes inside and applies routed_scaling_factor."""
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    model.experts = layer = _RoutedExperts()
+    layer.quant_method.is_monolithic = True
+    layer.routed_scaling_factor = 1.0
+    for key, value in routing.items():
+        setattr(layer, key, value)
+
+    def forward_monolithic(x, router_logits):
+        s13, s2 = layer._kernel_scales
+        top = torch.softmax(router_logits.float(), dim=-1).topk(layer.top_k, dim=-1)
+        out = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], HID)
+        for r in range(x.shape[0]):
+            for weight, e in zip(top.values[r].tolist(), top.indices[r].tolist(), strict=True):
+                if weight:
+                    w13, w2 = layer.w13_weight.data[e], layer.w2_weight.data[e]
+                    out[r] += weight * mxfp8_moe_expert_reference(x[r : r + 1], w13, s13[e], w2, s2[e])[0]
+        return (out * layer.routed_scaling_factor).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    layer.forward_monolithic = forward_monolithic
+    return model
